A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GTA1. All pages, including v1's end-of-paper examples and v4's Appendices A–D, are readable, and the methods, equations, experiments and retained figures can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original grounding and OSWorld results in Tables 1–4, reward and scaling ablations, and an AndroidWorld experiment in Section 4.3.

after.justification: v4 retains original empirical results and reports additional 32B grounding, OSWorld-Verified and WindowsAgentArena results in Tables 1–5.

M1.justification: Equation (4) changes the stated training loss from an unclipped probability-ratio-weighted advantage to a minimum of unclipped and clipped surrogates. The planning–judging–grounding procedure, annotation filtering and click reward remain unchanged. This establishes a limited revision to the reported objective, without establishing whether the implementation changed.

E1.justification: v4 adds WindowsAgentArena evaluation, extending actual agent task execution to Windows applications beyond v1's OSWorld and AndroidWorld experiments. The three grounding benchmarks are retained. OSWorld-Verified is described as an environment/evaluator refinement, rather than clearly establishing another task domain.

E2.justification: OpenCUA-32B is added to all three grounding comparisons. The agent comparisons expand to include Agent S2.5 and CoAct-1 on OSWorld-Verified, while the new WindowsAgentArena comparison includes Kimi-VL, WAA and Jedi. These are reported comparators, not merely additional citations.

E3.justification: The 32B configuration changes from Qwen2.5-VL-32B initialization, a 10^-6 learning rate and batch size 128 to OpenCUA-32B initialization, 10^-5 and batch size 256. v4 drops the proposed 72B configuration and adds GPT-5 planner configurations, OSWorld-Verified evaluation and original-instruction OSWorld-G evaluations alongside refined instructions. These materially change the reported experimental settings.

E4.justification: Table 3 adds paired OSWorld-G instruction-condition comparisons, providing limited evidence about sensitivity to instruction detail: GTA1-7B scores 55.1% with original instructions and 67.7% with refined instructions. The reward ablation, candidate-count/horizon study, AndroidWorld reasoning comparison and two trajectory case studies are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-evaluation run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests for its results. The rollout counts and newly disclosed parallel environment counts are training/infrastructure settings, not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 replace the 32B results, including ScreenSpot-Pro 53.6% to 63.6%, under the changed initialization and training settings; these are not same-setting gains. The 72B results are removed. Table 1 also corrects GTA1-7B's Scientific Text/Icon entries from 31.8/76.4 to 76.4/31.8. New results include 62.0% on OSWorld-Verified for GTA1-32B with GPT-5 and 51.2% on WindowsAgentArena with o3.

T1.justification: Equation (4) substantively revises the mathematical objective by introducing the clipped surrogate and clipping parameter epsilon. Equations (1)–(3) retain equivalent filtering, reward and normalization definitions despite notation changes. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The contribution list and central claims remain the same: per-step candidate sampling and judging improve planning, while click-reward reinforcement learning enables effective grounding without explicit reasoning. The added configurations and benchmarks mainly extend evidence for the retained grounding and agent-performance claims.

C2.justification: Section 5 newly acknowledges a concrete failure condition: difficulty selecting custom foregrounds and backgrounds during image editing. The explanations concerning objective alignment, reasoning in static versus dynamic environments, and cascading failures otherwise remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendices B–D substantially expand the short implementation description in v1. They disclose optimizer and rollout parameters, hardware and training times, image/bounding-box resizing, the 70K training sample description, evaluation serving arrangements, and exact grounding, planning, selection and ablation prompts. The linked code/model repository is unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds references supporting the expanded experiments and implementation, including OpenCUA, WindowsAgentArena, CoAct-1, Kimi-VL, additional training datasets and vLLM. The grounding/two-stage/native-agent taxonomy and the main positioning relative to previous reasoning-based grounding work remain intact.

P1.justification: The abstract and substantial portions of the introduction and related work are rewritten and condensed. Implementation information is reorganized into a structured appendix with a contents page and training, evaluation and prompt subsections; the conclusion gains a limitations component. These changes extend beyond simply inserting new results.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn with revised model series and an OSWorld-Verified panel. Table 3 expands and identifies instruction conditions, and Table 4 gains a second benchmark column. v4 adds WindowsAgentArena, training-parameter and extensive boxed prompt tables. Figures 5–6 are retained and relocated into the appendix, not new case studies.

improvement.justification: Appendices B–D supply crucial training, preprocessing, deployment and prompt information missing from v1, substantially improving reproducibility. Table 3 also identifies instruction conditions previously left unmarked, making comparisons more interpretable. Windows evaluation and a concrete limitation strengthen validation. Stale prose in Section 4.2 and unresolved appendix references remain, but do not outweigh these gains; the higher 32B scores alone do not establish improvement because its configuration changed.
